## Problem statement

Write pytest unit tests for the merge helper script (`scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py`), test-first, against the planned API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tests import and exercise the merge helper's public functions directly.
- [ ] Tests cover merged `providers`: tracked provider added to an existing destination, and tracked provider updating an existing destination provider while preserving the rest.
- [ ] Tests cover `modelOverrides` union — tracked overrides merge with existing overrides.
- [ ] Tests cover `enabledModels` union — deduplicated, local patterns preserved.
- [ ] Tests cover local-only providers preserved untouched.
- [ ] Tests cover the timestamped `models.json.bak.<ts>` / `settings.json.bak.<ts>` backup written once before the first modification.
- [ ] Tests cover atomic write (temp file + rename), and fail-open on unparseable JSON (file untouched, non-zero exit).
- [ ] Tests cover idempotent re-run — second run leaves both files unchanged.
- [ ] Tests run under `stdin=/dev/null` (non-interactive-safe) and use temporary directories, never the real filesystem.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py` — new test file

data.description:
## Summary

Replace the substring-based dedupe (_has_existing_worklog_item) with an exact, line-independent identity for refactor-filed smells (parent SA-0MW7Z1AU1006UT9C). A finding's identity is (repository-relative path, rule/smell code) — never the line number, never an absolute path — carried in a machine-readable marker in the item description so lookups survive line drift, worktree-path drift and title truncation.

## Key Files

- skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py — identity helper, marker emission, _has_existing_worklog_item replacement
- skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py — batch grouping so same-identity smells file one item
- tests/test_refactor/test_workitem_creation.py, tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py — F1 suite

## Target outcome

Every refactor item carries a stable identity + fingerprint, and the pre-creation guard matches on exact identity instead of substrings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Identity of a finding is (repo-relative path, rule/smell code); line number and absolute path are excluded. Paths are normalised with the existing shared _repo_relative_path helper from SA-0MW7Z11PV003V7O2 (worktree prefixes stripped).
- New items embed the identity as a machine-readable marker (Refactor-Finding-Key: <code>:<path>), a content fingerprint (Refactor-Fingerprint: sha256 of target-file content + rule set, per AC1 of the re-verification item SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3), and the full affected-line list (Refactor-Affected-Lines: n, m) so consolidation loses no diagnostic detail (AC5).
- _has_existing_worklog_item is replaced by an exact-key lookup: one "wl list Refactor-Finding-Key: --json" call, local regex parse (audit-side CFP-Chore-Key precedent), filter to non-terminal items only, exact key comparison after path normalisation — no substring matching anywhere.
- Batch creation (create_smell_work_items) groups same-identity findings into one item whose affected-line list is the union (covers parent AC6 case 1: same smell twice in one run; AC5 line-level reporting).
- The F1 regression suite for identity, markers, fingerprint and normalisation passes.
- skill/refactor/SKILL.md documents the identity definition, marker format, and fingerprint semantics.

## Constraints

- Identity must remain stable when the same file is scanned from an implement worktree and from the main checkout (reuse _repo_relative_path; do not duplicate it).
- Marker must sit near the top of the description so truncation cannot hide it; wl list --json returns full descriptions (verified).

## Risky assumptions

- Files whose path contains a colon are out of scope (matches the audit-side CFP-Chore-Key precedent); documented in SKILL.md.
- Fingerprint schema: sha256 of file bytes + rule code at filing time; may need to align exactly with SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3 when that item lands — the marker is additive and will be consumed there.

## Impact

Duplicate filings stop: the same smell collapses to one tracked item with all its lines, regardless of which worktree or scan produced it.
data.title: Machine-readable finding identity marker

data.comment:
Implementation decisions (F2):
- Identity: `<code>:<repo-relative-path>`; line number and absolute/worktree prefix excluded. Path reuse of shared `_repo_relative_path` (SA-0MW7Z11PV003V7O2). `build_finding_key`/`parse_finding_key` expose build/parse.
- Markers emitted near the top of the description: `Refactor-Finding-Key`, `Refactor-Fingerprint` (sha256 of file bytes + NUL + rule code; path not hashed so worktree/main agree), `Refactor-Affected-Lines` (deduplicated sorted union).
- `_has_existing_worklog_item` replaced by `_find_existing_worklog_item`: one `wl list Refactor-Finding-Key: --json` call, local regex parse, non-terminal filter (completed/deleted excluded), exact key comparison after path normalisation. No substring matching remains.
- Batch creation groups by identity (`group_smells_by_identity`) and files one item per identity with the union of lines; `create_smell_work_items_mapped` gives refactor.py an identity→item mapping so REFACTOR comment injection no longer relies on positional indices.
- Repeat-occurrence comments (F4) and consolidation grouping (F5) are intentionally left to their sibling items (SA-0MWE1EGLM002KE7Z, SA-0MWE1ELZO004J1DY), whose contract tests remain guarded/skipped; cross-family twin suppression (F3) likewise remains for SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO.
- Risky assumption documented in SKILL.md: paths containing a colon are out of scope (split on first colon), matching the audit-side CFP-Chore-Key precedent.
- Changed-scope validation: 169 passed, 6 skipped (F3/F4/F5 guards); ruff check clean.
